submit.sidebar.title: What this platform does to protect you
submit.sidebar.short: Anonymous unless you choose otherwise. No IP address is stored.
submit.sidebar.g01.title: No IP address logging
submit.sidebar.g01.desc: OpenWhistle does not store your IP address, and its bundled web server configuration does not log it. On a work device or network, your employer may still see that you opened this site.
submit.sidebar.g02.title: Case number and secret PIN
submit.sidebar.g02.desc: After submitting you get a case number and a long secret PIN that only you have. You need both to open your report again; they cannot be recovered.
submit.sidebar.g03.title: No tracking
submit.sidebar.g03.desc: No analytics, tracking pixels or third-party requests. The only cookies are those the form and your language choice need to work.
submit.sidebar.g17.title: HinSchG deadlines
submit.sidebar.g17.desc: The reporting office must confirm receipt within 7 days and give feedback within 3 months. You can exchange messages with it here.
submit.sidebar.onion: Your employer's network can see that this site was visited, not what you send. On a work network, use Tor Browser and this address:

admin.telephone.title: Telephone reporting channel
admin.telephone.subtitle: HinSchG §16 Abs. 1 Nr. 2 requires that internal reporting channels include a telephone hotline option in addition to the written channel provided by OpenWhistle. This page guides you through setting up a compliant telephone reporting channel.
admin.telephone.legal_req.label: Legal requirement:
admin.telephone.legal_req.body.html: Organisations with 50 or more employees and all public authorities are legally required to offer at least two reporting channels — one of which must allow verbal (telephone) reporting pursuant to HinSchG §16 Abs. 1 Nr. 2. OpenWhistle fulfils the written channel; you must provide the telephone channel separately.
admin.telephone.checklist.title: Compliance checklist
admin.telephone.checklist.intro: Verify that your telephone reporting channel meets the following requirements:
admin.telephone.checklist.1: A dedicated telephone number is published internally and accessible to all employees.
admin.telephone.checklist.2: The channel is confidential — calls are handled by trained, impartial staff or an external ombudsman.
admin.telephone.checklist.3: The person answering is bound by a confidentiality obligation (§9 HinSchG).
admin.telephone.checklist.4: A verbal report can be transcribed and submitted to OpenWhistle under a case number by staff — with the whistleblower’s consent (§17 Abs. 1 HinSchG).
admin.telephone.checklist.5: The whistleblower is informed about the channel via internal communications, intranet, and/or poster.
admin.telephone.checklist.6: Call recordings, if any, are compliant with DSGVO and §9 HinSchG confidentiality provisions.
admin.telephone.checklist.7: The channel is operational during normal business hours (or 24/7 for critical industries).
admin.telephone.checklist.8: If using an external ombudsman, their engagement letter includes a DSGVO Art. 28 Data Processing Agreement (DPA).
admin.telephone.options.title: Implementation options
admin.telephone.options.internal.title: Internal hotline
admin.telephone.options.internal.body: Designate a trained employee (Compliance Officer, HR) as the channel operator. Assign a dedicated direct-dial number. Document the duty schedule.
admin.telephone.options.internal.note: Best for: organisations with an existing compliance or legal function.
admin.telephone.options.external.title: External ombudsman
admin.telephone.options.external.body: Engage a certified external ombudsman (Ombudsmann) or compliance service provider. They receive calls on your behalf and forward anonymised reports to OpenWhistle.
admin.telephone.options.external.note: Best for: smaller organisations or where impartiality is critical.
admin.telephone.integration.title: Integration with OpenWhistle
admin.telephone.integration.1.html: Staff enters the verbal report via OpenWhistle’s submission form. Ask the caller’s consent before creating the report on their behalf.
admin.telephone.integration.2.html: Select “Confidential” mode if the caller consents to having their name recorded, so that the whistleblower receives a dedicated case number.
admin.telephone.integration.3.html: Provide the case number and PIN to the caller so they can follow up on their report via the whistleblower status page.
admin.telephone.integration.4.html: Document the telephone report in the admin notes (never in the public message thread visible to the whistleblower).
admin.telephone.recording.title: Recording prohibition notice (§10 HinSchG)
admin.telephone.recording.warning.label: Important:
admin.telephone.recording.warning.body.h: §10 HinSchG prohibits the covert recording of verbal reports without the whistleblower’s explicit consent. Any recording must be disclosed at the start of the call and the whistleblower must actively agree. Covert recordings may lead to criminal liability under §201 StGB (violation of spoken word confidentiality).
admin.telephone.recording.script.intro: Recommended call opening script (adapt to your organisation):
admin.telephone.recording.script.text.ht: “Thank you for calling the confidential reporting channel of [Organisation Name]. This call is handled by [Name/Role], who is bound by strict confidentiality. Your report will be treated in accordance with the Hinweisgeberschutzgesetz (HinSchG). This call is not being recorded. You may remain anonymous. Please go ahead with your report.”
admin.telephone.refs.title: Legal references
admin.retention.title: Data retention policy
admin.retention.subtitle: Automatic deletion of closed reports after the configured retention period. Satisfies GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) storage limitation and HinSchG §11 Abs. 5.
admin.retention.enabled_notice: Retention is on by default since v1.5.0. A closed report is deleted {days} days after it was closed (HinSchG §11 Abs. 5: three years after the procedure concludes). OpenWhistle was released in 2026, so no installation holds a report closed that long ago — nothing has been deleted early, and the first deletions are years away.
admin.retention.disabled_notice.html: Retention is currently disabled. To enable automatic deletion, set RETENTION_ENABLED=true in your environment configuration. Optionally adjust RETENTION_DAYS (default: 1095 = 3 years).
admin.retention.how.title: How it works
admin.retention.how.1: Every day at 03:00 UTC the retention scheduler runs.
admin.retention.how.2.html: Reports with status “closed” whose closed_at timestamp is older than {days} days are permanently deleted.
admin.retention.how.3: All associated data is removed: messages, attachments, notes, audit-log references (case number preserved in the auto-deletion audit entry).
admin.retention.how.4.html: An immutable audit log entry (report.auto_deleted) is written for each deleted report, recording the case number, closed date, retention period, and compliance basis.
admin.retention.how.note.html: Note: Reports in any status other than “closed” are never auto-deleted, regardless of their age.
admin.retention.legal.title: Legal basis
admin.retention.legal.gdpr5.title: GDPR Art. 5(1)(e) — storage limitation
admin.retention.legal.gdpr5.body: Personal data must not be kept longer than necessary for the purpose for which it was collected. Retaining closed reports indefinitely would violate this principle.
admin.retention.legal.hinschg.title: HinSchG §11 Abs. 5 — documentation obligation
admin.retention.legal.hinschg.body.html: The documentation of a report must be deleted 3 years after the procedure is concluded; it may be kept longer only while that is necessary and proportionate. The default retention period of 1095 days (3 years) matches this deadline. Change RETENTION_DAYS only on specific legal advice.
admin.retention.legal.gdpr17.title: GDPR Art. 17 — right to erasure
admin.retention.legal.gdpr17.body: Individuals may request deletion of their personal data. The auto-deletion mechanism and the existing manual 4-eyes deletion workflow both support fulfillment of erasure requests.
admin.retention.config.title: Configuration reference
admin.retention.config.enabled.desc: Enable automatic deletion of aged closed reports.
admin.retention.config.days.desc: Days after closing before a report is auto-deleted.
admin.system.title: System & updates
admin.system.subtitle: Installed version and update status.
admin.system.disabled_notice.html: The update check is disabled. Set UPDATE_CHECK_ENABLED=true to let OpenWhistle check GitHub daily for new releases.
admin.system.privacy.title: Privacy
admin.system.privacy.body.html: When enabled, the update check performs a single request to GitHub's public releases API. It sends no instance or report data — only a standard HTTP request. The result is cached and refreshed once a day.
admin.system.config.title: Configuration
admin.system.config.enabled.desc: Enable the daily GitHub update check (opt-in; no data is sent to GitHub).
admin.system.integrity.title: File integrity
admin.system.integrity.note.html: Verifies application files against a manifest baked into this image at build time. This detects accidental modification, incomplete deployments, and corruption. It is not tamper-proof: an attacker able to write to the container could also alter the baseline manifest.
admin.system.integrity.unavailable_note: No integrity manifest is present. This is expected outside a released Docker image (e.g. local development).
